subject: DPA: retention/erasure terminology and evidence flow
content:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acme.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA retention / erasure language

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA earlier. Our security team has a few focused questions before we start redlining:

- Can you confirm how Redwood defines 'erasure' versus 'anonymization' in operational terms? We need precise language for the DPA (e.g., reversibility, hashable tombstones, residual backups).
- What are the operational windows for deleting: (a) inference KV cache / model prefixes, (b) telemetry and request logs, (c) backups / snapshots across regions?
- How will evidence of deletion be provided? We expect a signed artifact or certificate that includes what was deleted and timestamps.
- Are there any conditions (legal hold, law enforcement requests, or backup retention policies) where deletion can be delayed? If yes, what notice do you provide and how is that surfaced to customers?

Attached is a short spreadsheet capturing the specific fields our legal team would like addressed. If possible, we would like a proposed counter-language for the following items: 'erase', 'residency', and 'backup copy' definitions.

Can we aim to have Redwood's suggested language and an evidence playbook by EOD Tuesday? Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to go over if that's easier.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior Information Security Manager
Acme Corp

---

On Mon, 1 Apr 2029, jasmine.liu@redwood.com wrote:
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention / erasure language

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level responses inline below and we attached a draft redline with concrete suggested phrasing (Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx).

- Erasure vs Anonymization: Operationally, erasure = irreversible deletion of the data object such that it cannot be reconstructed from Redwood backups or caches; anonymization = irreversible transformation removing identifiers while retaining aggregate utility. We propose DPA language that defines erasure as: 'permanent removal of the specified data object from active storage, persistent caches, and customer-accessible backups, with verification artifacts produced as described in the Evidence section.'

- Windows:
  * KV cache / prefixes: ephemeral—tombstoned on request; typical surface-level removal within 0–2 hours; final eviction from persistent caches within 48 hours depending on workload.
  * Telemetry & request logs: 90 days by default for observability; amendments possible via annex.
  * Backups & snapshots: backups are scheduled weekly and retained for up to 30 days (business default), with restore windows during which deletion requires coordination (see Legal Hold).

- Evidence: We can provide a signed deletion certificate (JSON artifact with SHA-256 of object tombstone, timestamp, and operator id), plus an entry in the audit log showing the erasure operation. Our forensic playbook is attached (erase_proof_playbook.pdf).

- Holds/Delays: Deletion may be paused for lawful process or customer-requested legal hold. We propose a notice-of-delay clause that requires Redwood to notify the customer within 24 hours of any hold, including scope and expected duration.

Ben and Rishi are cc'd — Ben can propose the exact legal phrasing, Rishi can comment on the technical evidence artifacts.

If that timeline works I can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, contracts@acme.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention / erasure language

Priya / Jasmine —

Thanks — below are concrete redline suggestions we believe will be acceptable to both sides. I'm keeping the wording tight to reduce back-and-forth.

1) Definitions (proposed DPA text):
   - "Erase/Erasure": "The permanent removal of Customer Data such that Redwood has no means to reconstruct the original Customer Data from active storage, persistent caches, backups, or any other storage mechanism controlled by Redwood. Erasure does not include aggregated or anonymized derivatives that do not permit re-identification of the subject data."

   - "Anonymization": "Transformation of Customer Data to prevent re-identification of individuals or entities, where reversal is not feasible using commercially reasonable means."

   - "Backup Copy": "A point-in-time copy of Customer Data stored for recovery purposes; Backup Copies are subject to the Backup Retention Period and may be stored in alternate regions for redundancy."

2) Operational SLA for deletion requests:
   - "Redwood will take commercially reasonable steps to remove Customer Data from active systems and caches within 72 hours of a verified erasure request. For Backup Copies, Redwood will either (i) delete or cryptographically render unreadable the relevant Backup Copies within 30 days, or (ii) if immediate deletion is not technically feasible, mark Backup Copies as ineligible for restoration and enforce logical inaccessibility until physical deletion can be completed."

3) Evidence and Auditability:
   - "Upon completion of erasure activities, Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate (JSON) that includes: (a) identifier(s) of the erased object(s), (b) timestamp(s) of erasure action(s), (c) cryptographic hash of tombstone or deletion marker, and (d) operator/service id. Redwood will retain the audit record for 12 months and make it available to the Customer under NDA for compliance review."

4) Holds and Exceptions:
   - "Redwood may delay erasure to comply with legal obligations or valid governmental requests. Redwood will notify the Customer within 24 hours of becoming aware of any such request and will seek to scope and minimize the duration of any delay."

5) Limited onshore backup carveout (optional):
   - "Where required by Customer for regulatory reasons, Redwood can provide for an onshore Backup Copy with restricted access. Such onshore Backup Copies will be logically isolated and access-controlled; Redwood will document the access controls and will ensure access is only given for legally required purposes or as specified in an agreed legal hold process."

Rishi — two quick notes from the engineering side you may want to weigh in on: the 72-hour active deletion SLA is conservative; we can frequently do prefix eviction sooner but commit to 72 hours though provide monitoring hook. Also, for the Deletion Certificate, can we include an immutable log id (e.g., Kafka offset / audit id)?

Priya — I've attached a short playbook showing how the deletion certificate is generated in practice. Happy to adjust the SLA to 14 days for Backup Copies if that's a hard requirement for you, but we'd prefer 30 days as a default.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133

Attachment: erase_proof_playbook.pdf

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, contracts@acme.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention / erasure language

Thanks — this is very helpful and much more concrete than the initial draft. A few follow-ups before we proceed to legal redlines: 

- For the Deletion Certificate: Acme prefers a signed JSON that includes the immutable audit id you mentioned (or an equivalent offset) and an assurance that the certificate is tamper-evident (digital signature). Can Redwood confirm the signing authority (Redwood keys) and whether we can verify signatures against a published Redwood public key?
- Backup Copy SLA: Acme is willing to accept a 30-day physical deletion window only if we receive an intermediate confirmation at day 14 that the Backup Copy has been marked ineligible for restoration and that access controls are enforced (including a human-readable statement of who has access). If possible, add that as a milestone.
- Onshore backups: we will need a short appendix describing the access control model for any onshore Backup Copies (roles, auditability, and legal hold procedures).

If you can incorporate those three points into the redline I'll circulate to our procurement and legal teams. Also please send the public key or the verification endpoint for the certificate signatures.

Priya
